# forge-kernel Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json for FK-01 to FK-04; hand-authored since FK-05, when the kernel left the Prism journey (one decision per app) to hold the capability gate. Change app/src and this file together. -->

## Purpose

Forge kernel: Decide the next build phase of a Hologram Forge app from its current phase and the event that just happened, and decide whether an origin may use an effect.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never proved when phase is not proved and event is not attest

The app SHALL NOT answer `proved` when phase is not proved and event is not attest, because the badge must never say proved unless Lean attested the current rules.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `drafting check` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `proved`
- **AND** the app answers `checked`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never published when phase is not proved and phase is not published

The app SHALL NOT answer `published` when phase is not proved and phase is not published, because an unproved app must never be published.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `drafting check` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `published`
- **AND** the app answers `checked`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Always drafting when event is edit

The app SHALL answer `drafting` when event is edit, because a proof must never outlive the rules it was about.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `proved edit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `drafting`
- **AND** the app answers `drafting`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never proving when phase is drafting

The app SHALL NOT answer `proving` when phase is drafting, because Lean must never run on rules that failed or skipped the check.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `drafting check` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `proving`
- **AND** the app answers `checked`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-001 drafting when event is edit

The app SHALL answer `drafting` when event is edit, because any edit invalidates the check and the proof.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `proved edit` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `drafting`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 checked when event is check and phase is drafting

The app SHALL answer `checked` when event is check and phase is drafting and no earlier rule matches, because a passing check moves a draft forward.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `drafting check` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `checked`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 proving when event is approve and phase is checked

The app SHALL answer `proving` when event is approve and phase is checked and no earlier rule matches, because approval starts Lean on checked rules only.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `checked approve` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `proving`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 proved when event is attest and phase is proving

The app SHALL answer `proved` when event is attest and phase is proving and no earlier rule matches, because only Lean's attestation marks the rules proved.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `proving attest` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `proved`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 checked when event is fail and phase is proving

The app SHALL answer `checked` when event is fail and phase is proving and no earlier rule matches, because a failed proof returns to checked so the user can fix the rules.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `proving fail` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `checked`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: REQ-006 published when event is publish and phase is proved

The app SHALL answer `published` when event is publish and phase is proved and no earlier rule matches, because only proved apps are published.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `proved publish` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `published`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: REQ-007 drafting when phase is drafting

The app SHALL answer `drafting` when phase is drafting and no earlier rule matches, because any other event leaves the phase unchanged.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule7`).

#### Scenario: REQ-007 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `drafting publish` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `drafting`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: REQ-008 checked when phase is checked

The app SHALL answer `checked` when phase is checked and no earlier rule matches, because any other event leaves the phase unchanged.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule8`).

#### Scenario: REQ-008 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `checked attest` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `checked`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: REQ-009 proving when phase is proving

The app SHALL answer `proving` when phase is proving and no earlier rule matches, because any other event leaves the phase unchanged.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule9`).

#### Scenario: REQ-009 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `proving check`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `proving`, decided by REQ-009

### Requirement: REQ-010 proved when phase is proved

The app SHALL answer `proved` when phase is proved and no earlier rule matches, because any other event leaves the phase unchanged.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule10`).

#### Scenario: REQ-010 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `proved check`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `proved`, decided by REQ-010

### Requirement: Otherwise published

The app SHALL answer `published` when no rule matches, because a published app stays published until it is edited.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `published wait` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `published`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `drafting check` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `checked`, decided by REQ-002, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 2 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `drafting`, `checked`, `proving`, `proved`, `published`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `phase` | `drafting`, `checked`, `proving`, `proved`, `published` | the build phase the app is in now |
| `event` | `check`, `approve`, `attest`, `fail`, `publish`, `edit`, `wait` | what just happened: the spec passed its check, the user approved, Lean attested the proof, the proof failed, the user published, the user edited the rules, or nothing |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `drafting` | the rules are new or changed and not yet checked |
| `checked` | the rules are consistent and the examples pass |
| `proving` | Lean is proving the guarantees |
| `proved` | Lean proved every guarantee for the current rules |
| `published` | the proved app is published |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 2 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

### Requirement: Capability gate, deny by default

A request `gate ORIGIN EFFECT RECORD GRANTED DENIED` asks whether ORIGIN (`forge`, `preview` or `published`) may use EFFECT (`store`, `fetch`, `infer`, `build`, `frame` or `serve`). RECORD says whether a grant record exists for that origin, GRANTED whether it grants the resource, and DENIED whether it denies it, each `yes` or `no`. The app SHALL answer `allow` or `deny`.

With no grant record, only Forge itself may act, and never by fetch. With a record, a denial always wins, and otherwise the grant decides.

#### Scenario: A preview without a grant cannot fetch

- **WHEN** the request is `gate preview fetch no no no`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`

#### Scenario: A granted preview fetch is allowed

- **WHEN** the request is `gate preview fetch yes yes no`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `allow`

#### Scenario: A denial wins over a grant

- **WHEN** the request is `gate preview fetch yes yes yes`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`

### Requirement: Never admitted outside Forge without a record

The gate SHALL NOT answer `allow` for a preview or published app when no grant record exists, because a forgotten record must never open a door.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (FK-05, theorem `noRecordOnlyForgeHolds`).

### Requirement: Never a fetch without a record

The gate SHALL NOT answer `allow` for a fetch when no grant record exists, Forge included, because every network request must be named by a grant.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (FK-06, theorem `noRecordNoFetchHolds`).

### Requirement: Deny wins

The gate SHALL NOT answer `allow` when the grant record denies the resource, because a denial must not depend on the order of entries.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (FK-07, theorem `denyWinsHolds`).

### Requirement: Outside Forge, only a grant admits

The gate SHALL NOT answer `allow` for a preview or a published app unless its record grants the resource, because generated code holds no authority of its own.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (FK-08, theorem `outsideForgeNeedsGrantHolds`).

### Requirement: No preview fetch without a grant

The gate SHALL NOT answer `allow` for a preview fetch unless granted, because a preview must not send the user's data anywhere unasked.

Verified: proved by Lean for every request (FK-09, theorem `previewNoNetworkWithoutGrantHolds`).

## Out of scope

- It decides the build phase and whether an effect is admitted. It performs no effect: storage, network, inference and the screen belong to the runner that asks it.
- Matching a request's origin against a list of granted endpoints is not modeled yet; the runner reduces it to GRANTED and DENIED.
- Events arrive one at a time; the caller keeps the current phase.

## Examples

- `drafting check` gives `checked`
- `checked approve` gives `proving`
- `proving attest` gives `proved`
- `proved publish` gives `published`
- `proved edit` gives `drafting`
- `proving fail` gives `checked`
- `drafting publish` gives `drafting`
- `checked attest` gives `checked`
- `published wait` gives `published`
- `gate forge store no no no` gives `allow`
- `gate forge fetch no no no` gives `deny`
- `gate preview fetch yes yes no` gives `allow`
- `gate published serve yes yes no` gives `allow`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proofs are about `judge` and `gateAllows`, the functions the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.

## Files

- `src/ForgeKernel.lex.tex` is the LexLean model, hand-authored since FK-05. It is the single source of the app.
- `src/ForgeKernelProofs.lex.tex` holds the theorems.
